TRADING PSYCHOLOGY
What is FOMO (Fear of Missing Out)?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

DETAILED DEFINITION

FOMO means fear of missing out. In market discussions it can describe concern about missing apparent gains or pressure to imitate a publicly shared trade. The label does not diagnose a condition, identify someone’s motives from their purchase or measure future returns. Selectively published gains omit unknown losses, costs and unsuccessful participants. A learner can record what was known before a simulated decision and what was learned later, keeping the price outcome separate from the quality of the reasoning. No neurological claim, universal loss rate or promise that journaling improves returns is established here.

HOW IT WORKS

FOMO is the anxiety-driven urge to trade because a price is moving or others appear to be profiting. The emotion does not identify a market top or establish a measured win rate.

KEY POINTS
Emotional response to seeing rapid price increases
Emotion alone does not establish where a market top is or a measured loss probability
Combat FOMO with pre-defined trading plans and alerts
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare the recorded reason for a virtual decision with the information available at that time. The exercise does not diagnose a person or distinguish professionals from amateurs.

Worked exercise and its limits

Write down what information was available before an imagined purchase and what was learned later. Separate a rising price from a claim that everyone else profited. This record cannot diagnose a person or establish the effect of an emotion on future prices.

SEC Investor.gov — investment risk (background, not validation of a strategy)
